newsitem.title: USA: Schering-Plough net up on sales surge.
newsitem.headline: Schering-Plough net up on sales surge.

text.p: Schering-Plough Corp. Thursday reported strong first-quarter profits as U.S. and worldwide sales of its pharmaceutical products rose sharply.
The drug company said net income rose to $375 million, or 1.03 a share, for the quarter ending March 31, from $327 million, or 89 cents a share, in the 1996 period.
Sales rose 13 percent to $1.6 billion from $1.4 billion, with a stronger U.S. dollar reducing the latest figure by about 3 percentage points.

"Schering- Plough achieved a solid performance in the first quarter, led by strong gains in our worldwide pharmaceuticals business," said Richard Jay Kogan, president and chief executive of the Madison, N.J.-based company.
"All of the company's major business components -- worldwide pharmaceuticals, animal health and HealthCare Products -- recorded higher sales vs. the prior year."
Worldwide ethical pharmaceutical sales grew by 14 percent, led by the Claritin line of nonsedating antihistamines and Intron A, an antiviral/anticancer agent.
First-quarter worldwide sales of Claritin surged 49 percent to $353 million. Sales of Intron A grew 19 percent to $143 million.
U.S. sales of prescription pharmaceuticals were up 21 percent in the 1997 first quarter.

International ethical pharmaceutical sales in the 1997 first quarter rose 6 percent. Higher sales were led by Claritin; Intron A; Losec, an anti-ulcer agent; and Elocon, a medium-potency topical steroid. Sales of respiratory products in Japan rose in anticipation of a stronger allergy season.
The company's growing worldwide animal health business surged 30 percent, mainly driven by higher worldwide sales of Nuflor, a broad-spectrum antibiotic for bovine respiratory disease.

Sales for Schering-Plough HealthCare Products rose 6 percent in the 1997 first quarter, largely due to strong sales of foot care products, benefiting from the addition of Dyna Step Inserts to the Dr. Scholl's foot care line, it said.
Schering-Plough's stock rose 50 cents to $75.875 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning.
